items.title: Charrettes (Design Sketching): ½ Inspiration, ½ Buy-In
items.summary: Design charrettes inspire design sketches and ideas, include more people in the design process, explore and expose goals and objectives of colleagues in multiple functional roles, and drive off designer’s block.

items.title: The Most Important Usability Activity
items.summary: What's worth the most: field studies or user tests? Depends on your company's usability maturity, but user testing is the safe bet if you can do only one thing.

items.title: Parallel & Iterative Design + Competitive Testing = High Usability
items.summary: 3 methods for increasing UX quality by exploring and testing diverse design ideas work even better when you use them together.

items.title: Corporate UX Maturity: Stages 5-8
items.summary: An organization that reaches the 'managed UX' stage still has far to go to reach UX nirvana. Attaining these higher maturity levels requires many years of effort.

items.title: Corporate UX Maturity: Stages 1-4
items.summary: As their UX approach matures, organizations typically progress through the same sequence of stages, from initial hostility to widespread reliance on user research.

items.title: Preface to the 2002 Reprint of "Coordinating User Interfaces for Consistency"
items.summary: Preface to the 2002 reprint of Jakob Nielsen's classic book from 1989 about user interface consistency.
